metaDescription: Five countertop nugget ice makers at or under $200, from a GE Profile Opal Mini to Silonn and Euhomy models, compared on output, tank, noise and cleaning.
expertTake: The GE Profile Opal Mini is the top pick because its top-fill reservoir and 36 pounds a day come from a maker with a long service network. The Silonn is the value choice, with a handled basket and a quiet profile. Anyone who wants a large party supply or a fully stocked bin should skip countertop nugget machines and look at undercounter units.
introParagraphs: Soft, chewable nugget ice is made differently from ordinary cubes. A cold cylinder freezes a thin layer of water, an auger scrapes it off and presses it into airy pellets, which is why the ice absorbs drink flavor and is so easy to chew.

Prices move, and the $200 cap here reflects Amazon listing prices when this guide was updated. At this level you are buying a countertop machine with a small reservoir and basket, so the questions that matter are daily output, cleaning habits and how loud the auger is in a kitchen.

products.name: GE Profile Opal Mini Nugget Ice Maker, 36 lb per Day
products.description:
The Opal Mini is a compressor-and-auger nugget machine scaled down for a countertop. It lists up to 36 pounds of ice a day, with first ice ready in about five minutes, which is the quickest start in this lineup. A top-fill station lets you pour water straight into the reservoir, so you do not have to lift a tank off the side.

Compared with the Silonn, the Opal Mini gives up a handled basket in exchange for the faster first batch and the larger service network behind the GE name. Compared with the two Euhomy models at similar output, it offers a more finished shell and a brand that stocks parts. The ice itself is the same style as every other pick: airy, crunchy and slow to dilute.

Ownership comes down to water and cleaning. Fill with filtered water to protect the evaporator, and run the cleaning cycle with a descaler monthly if your supply is hard. Leave 6 inches of clearance around the vents, because compressor heat in a closed cabinet cuts output sharply.
products.bestFor: Households that want a trusted brand and the fastest first batch.
pros: About 5 minutes to the first ice
Top-fill reservoir is easy to refill
Brand with parts and service reach
36 lb per day rating is the highest here
cons: Rated output assumes a cool room
Auger noise is audible in a quiet kitchen

products.name: Silonn Countertop Nugget Ice Maker with Handled Basket
products.description:
The Silonn is built around a detachable ice basket with a handle, which makes carrying ice to a table or cooler easy. It produces nugget ice in about six minutes and markets a quiet running profile. The cost side shows up in the shell: it is simple plastic, and the brand has a shorter track record than the GE.

Next to the Opal Mini, the handled basket is the big convenience win, and it is a more pleasant machine to serve from during a small gathering. The tradeoff is the less detailed spec sheet and the lack of a stated daily output on the listing, which makes it harder to predict how many full baskets you will get in an afternoon. A pour-in reservoir needs refilling more often than the larger Euhomy tanks.

Care is routine. Empty the water and ice after party use, wipe the basket, and run a descaling cycle when the ice tastes flat. Keep it on a level surface and give it room at the sides so the compressor can breathe.
products.bestFor: Buyers who want an easy-to-carry basket and a lower listing price.
pros: Handled basket carries ice to the table
Lowest in the lineup on price tier

products.name: Kismile 35 lb Stainless Countertop Nugget Ice Maker
products.description:
The Kismile combines a stainless body with a 1.1 liter tank and a rating of up to 35 pounds a day. A five-second press of the power button starts a self-cleaning cycle, which simplifies the routine for users who forget maintenance. The steel shell resists fingerprints better than plastic and looks at home near a coffee setup.

It offers slightly less output than the GE Opal Mini and a smaller tank than the Euhomy with a 1.2 quart reservoir, so it sits in the middle. The upside is the build: stainless is easier to wipe clean and looks tidy. The downside is that stainless fronts get dents and the steel conducts heat, so the side panels warm during long runs.

Use filtered water, and treat the self-clean as a rinse rather than a descale. Descale every month or two if your water is hard. The sealed top cover should be wiped dry to prevent mold in the corners.
products.bestFor: Kitchens where appearance matters and cleaning has to be quick.
pros: Compact 1.1 L tank fits tight counters
cons: Sides warm up in long runs

products.name: Euhomy Countertop Nugget Ice Maker with Handle, 34 lb
products.description:
This Euhomy has a carry handle, a removable top cover and a 1.2 quart tank, which makes it the easiest to move between counters. It lists 34 pounds a day and as little as six minutes to first ice, close to the Opal Mini's output. The removable top is a hygiene benefit, since you can wipe the inside of the lid.

Set beside the Kismile it has a slightly larger tank, and against the Silonn it has a stated output, which is a point for planning. The tradeoff is the lighter-weight shell and the usual Euhomy complaint that the auger is audible. Place it on a rubber mat to reduce vibration noise.

Maintenance is the standard filtered water routine. Run the auto-clean cycle with a descaler monthly and dry the lid after cleaning. The handle is plastic, so lift with the other hand under the base when the tank is full.
products.bestFor: People who move the machine around or like to open and wipe the lid.
cons: Auger noise carries in small kitchens
Tank needs refills in long sessions

products.name: Euhomy 2026 Countertop Sonic Nugget Ice Maker, 35 lb
products.description:
This model lists 35 pounds a day and first ice in 5 to 7 minutes, with a dual-pump water system. The two pumps are meant to move water more reliably through the system, which should reduce dry-fill errors in daily use. It makes the same soft crunchy ice as the other picks.

The maker's own tip, to run two or three self-cleaning cycles after a deep descale, is a useful sign that the machine is sensitive to residue. Measured against the 34 pound Euhomy, it adds a pump and a slightly higher rating but no handle. Against the Opal Mini, it offers a similar start time with less brand support.

Use filtered water and descale every few weeks. Rinse thoroughly after any chemical descale, and run the self-clean cycle twice with clean water so the first batch of ice has no aftertaste.
products.bestFor: Heavy daily users who want a more robust water pump system.
cons: Residue after descaling needs extra rinses

buyingCriteria.explanation: A rated 34 to 36 pounds a day sounds large, but the basket holds only a small portion at once, so production stops when it fills. The GE Opal Mini and the Euhomy 35 pound model produce at about the same rate, and the rate matters most for a party where you scoop ice repeatedly. Measure your need as scoops per hour rather than pounds per day. A cool room helps the compressor, and a warm kitchen drops real output below the sticker figure. Start the machine an hour before guests arrive so the basket is already full, then scoop in batches instead of one cup at a time, because each scoop of warm hands and open lid melts a surprising amount of ice.

Reservoirs run from 1.1 liters on the Kismile to a 1.2 quart tank on the Euhomy handle model. A small tank empties in a few batches, and some machines shut off when water is low, which interrupts a session. The GE Opal Mini's top-fill design lets you pour from a pitcher without moving the unit. If you serve a family of four, keep a water jug nearby so you are not carrying the tank back and forth.

Nugget machines are louder than bullet makers because an auger turns inside a chilled cylinder. A rubber mat reduces vibration through the counter, and distance from the sink and cooking zone keeps splashes away. Quiet marketing on the Silonn should be taken as relative, since you will still hear a hum and a grinding click as ice is scraped. Never place it in a closed cabinet, because the compressor needs at least 6 inches of air at the sides.

A self-clean button flushes the water path but does not remove mineral scale. The Kismile has a five-second self-clean, and the Euhomy 2026 model advises extra rinse cycles after descaling. Scale on the evaporator cuts output and makes ice taste flat. Plan to descale with citric acid or a maker-approved cleaner every one to two months if your water is hard.

A stainless shell, as on the Kismile, resists fingerprints and cleans easily but dents. A plastic shell, as on the Silonn, is lighter and cheaper, and it can yellow over time. The lid design matters: a removable top cover, as on the Euhomy handle model, lets you wipe the inside where mold likes to form. Compare how much of the interior is reachable by hand.

The GE Profile Opal Mini comes from a manufacturer with a service network, which counts if the compressor or the auger fails after the first year. Smaller brands often depend on the seller for replacements. Check the return window and the warranty period before purchase, and keep the original box for at least the first month. A compressor failure outside warranty is usually not worth repairing at this price level. Register the serial number the day you unbox it, and test the unit through two full basket cycles inside the return window so that any buzzing compressor, leaking tank or auger that grinds dry is caught while a refund is simple.

specDecoder.meaning: A theoretical maximum under cool room and cool water conditions. In a warm kitchen the figure can drop by a quarter or more.
specDecoder.watchFor: The GE Opal Mini's 36 pounds and the Euhomy 35 pounds are best-case numbers.

specDecoder.meaning: How long the machine takes to produce the first batch after startup. It depends on the water temperature and room heat.
specDecoder.watchFor: The Opal Mini and Euhomy 2026 state about 5 minutes, but a warm start takes longer.

specDecoder.meaning: The amount of water available before a refill. A larger tank means fewer interruptions but a heavier unit.
specDecoder.watchFor: The Kismile's 1.1 L tank is the smallest listed, so it needs the most attention.

specDecoder.meaning: A top-fill reservoir accepts water without moving the machine. A side or removable tank needs lifting and carrying.
specDecoder.watchFor: Only the Opal Mini advertises top-fill convenience here.

specDecoder.meaning: A flush that circulates water to rinse the system. It does not dissolve scale on its own.
specDecoder.watchFor: The Kismile and the Euhomy models offer it, but all still need periodic descaling.

howWeEvaluated.title: Output and speed
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared stated daily output and first-ice time across the lineup, from the 34 pound Euhomy to the 36 pound GE. Where a listing gave no figure, as with the Silonn, we scored cautiously. Best-case numbers were treated as upper limits, not guarantees.

howWeEvaluated.title: Convenience design
howWeEvaluated.description: Top-fill access, handled baskets and carry handles were judged on how they affect daily use. The GE Opal Mini's top-fill and the Silonn's basket handle scored well. We also weighed removable lids and tank sizes.

howWeEvaluated.title: Cleaning and upkeep
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at self-clean cycles, lid access and descaling advice. A one-button clean on the Kismile reduces effort, while the Euhomy 2026 model's two-cycle rinse note signals a more demanding routine.

howWeEvaluated.title: Build and support
howWeEvaluated.description: Stainless, plastic and brand reach were weighed. The GE name carries a service advantage, and the smaller brands depend on return policies. Owner feedback patterns on auger noise informed the cons.

howWeEvaluated.title: Fit at the cap
howWeEvaluated.description: Each unit had to be at or under the cap on its live listing. We favored models that spend the budget on usable output and cleaning ease rather than decoration.

cards.label: Top-fill (GE Opal Mini)
cards.text: You pour water from a pitcher without moving the machine, which suits a fixed spot near a sink or fridge.

cards.label: Removable tank (Euhomy, Kismile)
cards.text: You carry the tank to the tap and back, which is simple but messy if the machine is full.

howToChoose.note: Pick the GE if the unit lives in one place, and a Euhomy if you want to fill at the sink.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: A machine that keeps up when you scoop several cups in a row. Look at first-ice time and the refill rhythm.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The GE Opal Mini starts fastest and holds a rating of 36 pounds. The Euhomy 35 pound model is close behind, with a dual pump to keep water flowing.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You need a continuous bin supply or a built-in storage bin. Undercounter nugget machines have larger bins and are a better fit for entertaining.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You only make a few cups of ice a day, in which case the Silonn handles it without the extra cost.

maintenance.why: It slows scale buildup on the evaporator. Hard tap water cuts output and flavor quickly.
Scale insulates the freezing cylinder. Use citric acid or the maker's descaler.
It flushes loose residue. Follow with a rinse cycle on fresh water.
Moisture breeds mold in corners. Dry with a clean cloth.
Standing water grows biofilm. Drain and dry the tank and bin.

faq.q: What makes nugget ice different from bullet ice?
faq.a: Nugget ice is scraped from a frozen cylinder and compressed into soft pellets, while bullet ice is frozen onto prongs and is harder. Nugget absorbs drink flavor and chews easily.

faq.q: What does the $200 cap buy compared with lower caps?
faq.a: It buys countertop machines rated 34 to 36 pounds a day with self-clean cycles and brand variety. The cap reflects listing prices when this guide was updated.

faq.q: How long do countertop nugget machines last?
faq.a: Three to five years is typical with filtered water and monthly descaling. The compressor and the auger are the likely failure points.

faq.q: Is 36 pounds a day really achievable?
faq.a: It is a best-case figure measured in a cool room with cold water. Expect a quarter less in a warm kitchen.

faq.q: Do I need to descale if I use the self-clean cycle?
faq.a: Yes. The self-clean cycle rinses the path but does not dissolve scale. Descale every month or two in hard water.

faq.q: Can I keep the ice in the machine?
faq.a: The ice slowly melts, and the water recycles to the tank. For storage, move ice to a freezer bin.
